entry.title: HKMA welcomes launch of Chongqing-Hong Kong cross-boundary data validation platform for secure data checks without moving original documents
entry.summary: HKMA welcomes launch of Chongqing-Hong Kong Cross-boundary Data Validation Platform HKMA · Oct 14, 2026 · Crypto On 14 October 2026, Chongqing and Hong Kong authorities launched the Chongqing-Hong Kong Cross-boundary Data Validation Platform (CQ-HK DVP), which uses blockchain technology and hash values to verify customer-submitted data without transferring or storing original documents across the border. The platform will initially support cross-boundary financial use cases, such as account opening and loan applications, building on the Shenzhen-Hong Kong platform.

entry.title: Hong Kong SFC strengthens targeted tools for IPO-related and other corporate misconduct
entry.summary: SFC proceeds to strengthen targeted tools to tackle IPO-related and other corporate misconduct SFC · Oct 13, 2026 The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) has published its consultation conclusions and will amend the Securities and Futures (Stock Market Listing) Rules to strengthen tools for handling IPO cases and post-IPO matters. The amendments allow conditions on listing applicants and post-listing conditions on listed issuers as an alternative to immediate trading suspension, and streamline resumption procedures. A new independent merits review mechanism through the Securities and Futures Appeals Tribunal will also be introduced. The SFC expects the amendments to take effect in the first quarter of 2027, subject to the legislative process. entry.summary: SFC approves six securities registrars for upcoming uncertificated securities market regime SFC · Oct 13, 2026 The SFC approved six companies as approved securities registrars effective 16 November 2026, when the uncertificated securities market regime takes effect. Listed issuers must always have an ASR to maintain their register, and existing issuers must participate within five years. entry.title: SFC to upgrade Hong Kong's retail fund rules
entry.summary: SFC to proceed with enhancements to Hong Kong’s retail fund regime code SFC · Oct 8, 2026 The Securities and Futures Commission will implement changes to the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds governing SFC-authorised retail funds. The changes add a Value-at-Risk approach for derivative exposure, simplify requirements for management companies and feeder funds, and strengthen liquidity risk management and money market fund safeguards. The revised codes take effect on 1 November 2026, with a 12-month transition period for existing funds. The SFC found the firm conducted no due diligence or testing on customer supplied systems used by 160 clients and did not properly monitor deposits and suspicious trading in eight client accounts.
